books.title: Test Theory Book
text:
Chapter 1: The Notes
The musical alphabet has seven letters. An octave is the same note twelve frets higher. Octave shapes help you find notes on the neck.
Octave shapes on the fretboard: two strings up and two frets up. Crossing the B string adds one fret. Practise octave shapes every day; the octave is the same note.

Chapter 2: CAGED
The CAGED system links five chord shapes: the C shape, A shape, G shape, E shape and D shape. CAGED shapes share their roots.

Chapter 3: Pentatonic scales
The minor pentatonic scale has five notes. The pentatonic box at fret 5 is the first one most players learn. Pentatonic licks.

books.title: Test Licks Book
text: Lick 1: a bend and release in A minor pentatonic. Bends need control.
Lick 2: hammer-ons and pull-offs, legato phrasing over a shuffle.
